qc.label_under_test: On the word right after me or us that opens a description of me or us (often 'as', 'a', 'for', 'my' or 'our') when a characterisation bounces back: an earlier clause has me or us characterising another person or group (seeing, regarding, calling or thinking them something, or praising, admiring, criticising, thanking, rewarding or punishing them for something), and the next clause has that person or group characterise me or us in the same way. Weaker: the same two-way swap between third-person pronouns. Silent: a returned attitude with no description of me or us after the pronoun (they trusted us, he feared me); a one-way characterisation of me or us with no earlier clause; me or us characterised first and then answering back; an ordinary returned action (visiting, lending, paying, hugging back); a characterisation aimed at a thing rather than a person.

neighbours.label: On the word right after me or us that opens a description of me or us (often 'as', 'a', 'for', 'my' or 'our') when a characterisation bounces back: an earlier clause has me or us characterising another person or group (seeing, regarding, calling or thinking them something, or praising, criticising or thanking them for something), and the next clause has that person or group characterise me or us in return, whether the returned description matches the first one or is different or opposite. Weaker: the same two-way swap between third-person pronouns. Silent: a returned attitude with no description of me or us after the pronoun (they trusted us); a one-way characterisation of me or us with no earlier clause; me or us characterised first and then answering back; an ordinary returned action (visiting, lending, paying back); a characterisation aimed at a thing rather than a person.
fire: We had always seen the villagers as strangers, and they in turn saw us as intruders.
I called him a genius, and he called me a fool for believing it.
We thanked the volunteers for their patience, and they thanked us for our generosity.
I regarded her as a rival, but she regarded me as a friend all along.
Our team praised the referees for their fairness, and the referees praised us for our sportsmanship.
I thought of my neighbor as rude, while he apparently thought of me as standoffish.
We criticized the council for its secrecy, and the council criticized us for our impatience.
I considered the new manager a breath of fresh air, and she considered me a reliable ally.
quiet: We had always seen the villagers as strangers, and they in turn never trusted us.
I called him a genius, and he called me back an hour later to say thanks.
We thanked the volunteers, and they visited us the following week with cookies.
I regarded her as a rival, and she lent me her notes anyway.
The referees praised us for our sportsmanship after the final match.
Everyone in the building thought of me as standoffish when I first moved in.
The council criticized us for our impatience, and we replied that the delays were unacceptable.
I considered the new manager a breath of fresh air, and she paid me back the money I had lent her.
